meta.purpose: Английские версии содержимого: разделов методологии и терминов глоссария. Содержимое наполняется командой seed_content на русском языке; английские версии хранятся отдельным файлом, чтобы их можно было править как текст и переносить между стендами вместе с кодом.
meta.matching: Записи сопоставляются по устойчивому идентификатору: код раздела методологии и адресный идентификатор термина. Идентификатор не зависит от языка.
meta.source: Поле source — отпечаток русского оригинала (apps.core.translation_qa.source_hash полей в порядке seed_content_en.TARGETS). Изменился оригинал — отпечаток не совпадает, перевод помечается устаревшим: seed_content_en --check и tests/unit/test_translations.py.

missing-values.title: Gaps and the source’s service codes
missing-values.summary: The values −99999999 and −77777777 in the Rosstat dataset mean that data are absent.
missing-values.limitations:
A withheld value cannot be recovered: only the source knows it.
For a year with withheld values the inequality measures show bounds rather than a single number.
missing-values.body:
The code −99999999 means “no data”. The code −77777777 means “value withheld for confidentiality”. On loading, both marks become an empty value, and the reason is kept as a quality flag. Zero is never put in place of a gap: zero is a valid value of many indicators.

On charts a gap is not bridged by a line. On the map a region without a value is hatched.

deduplication.title: One observation in different issues
deduplication.summary: If issues of publications disagree, the value from the latest one is in force, and earlier ones are kept in “Revisions”.
deduplication.limitations:
The value in force may change with the next issue.
Only revisions between issues included in the dataset are visible.
deduplication.body:
An observation is defined by the indicator, the breakdown, the territory and the year. One observation is printed in several issues, most often unchanged. If the value differs between issues, that is a revision. The value from the latest issue is in force, and earlier versions are kept.

Issues of Rosstat’s bulletin, of the GRP table and snapshots of Bank of Russia data are ordered by release date. For the compendia of the dataset the release date is taken as the end of the year of publication.

comparability-breaks.title: Comparability breaks
comparability-breaks.summary: The year from which a series cannot be compared with earlier years is taken from Rosstat’s notes and the footnotes to its tables.
comparability-breaks.limitations:
A break is detected from the text of a note: if the source did not describe a change, there is no mark.
The source does not publish the size of the jump at a break, so the series is not recalculated.
comparability-breaks.body:
Rosstat accompanies series with notes such as “from 2017 under the new methodology”. One note often describes several changes, so it is parsed part by part. For each part the kind of change and the year from which the series loses comparability are determined. Kinds of change: methodology, classification, territorial composition, scope of observed units, price base. A recalculation based on census results does not set a break.

A change in the composition of a district or the country changes only their values. A change for a region across such a mark is computed. A change in the composition of one region gives a mark to that region only.

The passport and the tiles do not compare across a break: instead of a change they name the year the counting rules changed. “Inequality” and “Convergence” warn about the break and offer the segment after it.

series-status.title: Publication status of series
series-status.summary: Series are marked with whether the source continues to publish them.
series-status.limitations:
The status is marked only for series checked by hand.
A discontinued series stays on the site with its last published year.
series-status.body:
The site works on the latest version of the dataset, and new versions are loaded as they appear. Rosstat publishes some indicators after the last year of the dataset too. These series are continued from the monthly bulletin and the GRP table.

Rosstat has stopped publishing regional demography: births, deaths, population, life expectancy, migration. These series are marked as getting no new values. Bank of Russia and Federal Tax Service series are updated with every release.

sources.title: Continuing series from Rosstat publications
sources.summary: Series that Rosstat publishes after the last year of the dataset are continued from its bulletin and the GRP table after a check over the common years.
sources.limitations:
Per-inhabitant values after the last population year are divided by the population of that year.
Values of the last year of an issue are preliminary and marked “prelim.”.
sources.body:
The annual value is taken from the publication if Rosstat publishes it. Otherwise RegionLens computes it: average income is averaged over four quarters, the average wage over twelve months. Such values are marked “calculated”.

Values of the publication for three common years are compared with the dataset region by region. Here N is the number of “region × year” pairs, and δ is the tolerance. The tolerance is 0.5 % for totals, 1 % for per-inhabitant values, 2 % for monthly and quarterly averages. For indices and shares it is 0.15 pp. With a smaller share of pairs within tolerance the link is conditional: a break is set at the joint.

The GRP table replaces the dataset’s values for all years, and earlier ones are visible in “Revisions”.

monthly.title: Monthly data: Bank of Russia, Federal Tax Service and Rosstat’s bulletin
monthly.summary: Mortgages, loans and small business are RegionLens series built from Bank of Russia and Federal Tax Service data, while wages, prices, unemployment and industry are also shown by month.
monthly.formula:
levels and sums: <math display="block"><mi>Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math>
shares, rates and indices: <math display="block"><mi>Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>)</mo></math>
monthly.limitations:
The Russia value of the SME register is the sum of the 85 regions of the directory, while the Federal Tax Service total is wider.
Bank of Russia series start in 2019, so five years are enough for comparisons.
monthly.body:
The Bank of Russia publishes lending and debt on loans to households and businesses by region. The Federal Tax Service SME register gives the number of SMEs and their employees on the 10th of each month. From Rosstat’s bulletin, wages, the price index, industrial production and unemployment are shown by month.

The annual value is built from the months of one release. Lending over a year is the sum of twelve months. Debt is taken as of 1 January of the following year. Term and rate are averaged over the months weighted by lending. An incomplete year gets no annual value. Month t is compared with the same month of the previous year.

own-data.title: Your own data
own-data.summary: The laboratory brings a user’s table to the form “territory × year × indicator” and computes the same on it as on the site’s series.
own-data.limitations:
Rows outside the directory are kept in the table but do not reach the map or the ranking.
With fewer than twenty regions, inequality and spatial analysis are not computed.
own-data.body: Territory labels are matched against the site’s directory, and the site asks about uncertain ones. Per-inhabitant and per-km² series are offered for regional sums. P is the average annual population. A recalculation is kept as a separate series marked “RegionLens calculation”. How each action works is explained next to it in the laboratory.

map-classes.title: Scale classes on the map
map-classes.summary: A colour on the map means a class, a range of values, and the way of dividing into classes is named in the legend.
map-classes.limitations:
With equal intervals one outlying region pushes the others into the lowest class.
The same colour means the same class, not the same value.
map-classes.body:
By default the regions are divided into five classes by quantiles. Each class holds about the same number of regions n / k. On the workspace you can choose from three to seven classes and another method. Equal intervals split the range into equal parts. Natural breaks (the Jenks method) follow the gaps in the distribution. Standard deviations count classes from the mean.

The change between two years is shown on a diverging scale with zero in the middle. A region without a value is hatched.

standing.title: “Better” and “worse”, and the core set
standing.summary: A region’s position is described in words by the share of regions with a worse value, and only indicators of the core set are assessed.
standing.limitations:
Indicators without a clear direction, such as loan size, are not assessed.
A place by an absolute quantity reflects the size of the region and is not assessed either.
standing.body:
Here m is the number of regions with a worse value, and n is the number of all regions. For indicators where growth is good, the worse value is the smaller one. For unemployment and the like it is the larger one.

Steps: from 0.85 “among the best values”, from 0.6 “better than in most regions”, from 0.4 “in the middle of the list”. Below 0.4 the position is “worse than in most”, up to 0.15 “among the worst”. A region’s strengths and weaknesses are in the best or worst 15 %.

The direction of the core set is checked by hand. For other series the site says “higher” and “lower”.

five-year-change.title: Change over five years and comparison with the country
five-year-change.summary: The value of the last year is compared with the value five years earlier: percentages in percentage points, money in real terms.
five-year-change.formula:
quantities of one sign: <math display="block"><mi>Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac></math>
percentages, in pp: <math display="block"><mi>Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msub></math>
with the country: <math display="block"><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mtext>RF</mtext></msub></mrow></mfrac></math>
five-year-change.limitations:
No change is given across a comparability break.
If there is no value from five years ago, no change is given either.
five-year-change.body:
Indicators in per cent change in percentage points. Positive quantities change in per cent. Quantities that pass through zero are compared by difference. A rate “% of the previous year” is not compared over five years. Monetary indicators are compared in real terms, and the change in roubles is given in brackets.

Percentages are compared with the country by a difference in points, other quantities by a ratio. From a one-and-a-half-fold gap the multiple is named. The tiles on the home page show the change over the last year.

real-terms.title: Monetary indicators in real terms
real-terms.summary: The change of monetary indicators is cleared of price growth using Rosstat’s indices.
real-terms.formula:
real-quantity index: <math display="block"><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><munderover><mo>∏</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>t</mi></munderover><mfrac><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mn>100</mn></mfrac></math>
price index: <math display="block"><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mfrac><mo>/</mo><munderover><mo>∏</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>t</mi></munderover><mfrac><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mn>100</mn></mfrac></math>
volume of the total: <math display="block"><mi>R</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mfrac><mo>·</mo><munderover><mo>∏</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>t</mi></munderover><mfrac><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mn>100</mn></mfrac><mo>/</mo><mfrac><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>s</mi></msub></mfrac></math>
real-terms.limitations:
For annual averages the December-to-December index is an approximation.
If the index is missing for at least one year, only the change in roubles is given.
real-terms.body:
R is the ratio of the value of year t to year s in constant prices. Indices to the previous year are multiplied over the years after the start. For wages and incomes per capita the real wage and real income indices I are used. GRP, investment and retail turnover are recalculated by volume indices V of the total X. Median income and wage, expenditure and housing prices are recalculated by the region’s consumer price index P.

Income in fixed baskets is income divided by the cost of the basket of the same year. This is a RegionLens calculation, not Rosstat’s purchasing power indicator.

similar-regions.title: Similar regions
similar-regions.summary: Similar regions are the closest ones by a combination of six key indicators brought to a standard form.
similar-regions.limitations:
The distance is good for ordering, not for claims like “twice as close”.
A region without one of the indicators is not compared, and shared borders are not taken into account.
similar-regions.body: The indicators are GRP per capita, population, life expectancy, per-capita income, the average wage and the poverty rate. Each is taken for the last complete year. Standardisation puts roubles and per cent on an equal footing. The six regions with the smallest distance are considered similar. The indicator with the largest difference is named next to each.

coverage.title: Suitability of a series for comparative analysis
coverage.summary: A series takes part in comparisons if it covers 80 % of the regions and at least 10 years.
coverage.formula:
region coverage: <math display="block"><mfrac><mtext>regions with a value</mtext><mn>85</mn></mfrac><mo>≥</mo><mn>0.8</mn></math>
years with such coverage: <math display="block"><mi>T</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>10</mn></math>
coverage.limitations:
Coverage is counted by the number of regions, not by their population.
Bank of Russia and Federal Tax Service series need five years: they do not exist before 2019.
coverage.body:
Other series are shown in the catalogue and on the indicator page. They are not offered in rankings and analysis tools: a ranking of a dozen regions does not describe the country.

The map, rankings and tools open on the last complete year of a series. A complete year is one with values for at least 80 % of the largest number of regions in the series. An incomplete last year stays in the year selection.

normalization.title: Bringing indicators to a comparable form
normalization.summary: Five methods bring indicators to a scale from 0 to 100, and the choice affects how robust the index is to outliers.
normalization.formula:
min-max: <math display="block"><mn>100</mn><mo>·</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>min</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>min</mi></mrow></mfrac></math>
z-score: <math display="block"><mn>50</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>50</mn><mo>·</mo><mfrac><mi>z</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mspace width="0.75em"></mspace><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>μ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>σ</mi></mrow></mfrac></math>
robust: <math display="block"><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>Me</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>IQR</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>1.349</mn></mrow></mfrac></math>
rank: <math display="block"><mn>100</mn><mo>·</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></math>
logarithmic: <math display="block"><mtext>min-max of</mtext><mspace width="0.17em"></mspace><mspace width="0.17em"></mspace><mi>ln</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mspace width="0.17em"></mspace><mi>x</mi></math>
normalization.limitations:
With min-max one outlying region squeezes the others into a narrow band.
The logarithmic scale applies only to positive quantities.
A series without a direction does not enter the index.
normalization.body:
On the scale, 100 is the best position. For indicators where less is better, the scale is reversed. Min-max keeps distances but depends on the extreme values. The z-score counts from the mean in standard deviations. Values beyond three deviations are clipped. The robust score counts from the median Me in interquartile ranges IQR. It is preferable for right-skewed per-capita indicators. The rank score uses only the order r. The logarithmic score compresses a long right tail.

The direction of the core set is set by hand, and for other series it is guessed from the wording.

weights.title: Determining indicator weights
weights.summary: Weights can be equal, expert, entropy-based, CRITIC-based or based on principal component loadings.
weights.limitations:
Objective weights reflect the spread of the data, not how much an indicator matters to people.
CRITIC measures association by the Pearson coefficient and misses non-linear relationships.
weights.body:
The weights sum to one. Equal weights make the indicators equally important. But three closely related indicators give their direction triple weight. Expert weights are set by the user. The entropy method gives more weight to an indicator that separates the regions more. CRITIC takes into account the spread σ and the correlation r, so a duplicating indicator gets less weight. Principal component weights rely on the structure of the relationships.

The robustness check recomputes the index with other scales and aggregations.

aggregation.title: Aggregating normalised values into an index
aggregation.summary: The index is built by additive or geometric aggregation, by TOPSIS or by the distance to a benchmark.
aggregation.formula:
additive: <math display="block"><mi>I</mi><mo>=</mo><munder><mo>∑</mo><mi>j</mi></munder><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></math>
geometric: <math display="block"><mi>I</mi><mo>=</mo><munder><mo>∏</mo><mi>j</mi></munder><msubsup><mi>x</mi><mi>j</mi><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msubsup></math>
TOPSIS: <math display="block"><mi>I</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>·</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></mrow></mfrac></math>
to the benchmark: <math display="block"><mi>I</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>100</mn><mo>·</mo><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>max</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac><mo>)</mo></math>
aggregation.limitations:
In geometric aggregation a zero score is replaced by a small positive quantity.
In TOPSIS and the distance to a benchmark a gap is replaced by the mean for the calculation.
aggregation.body:
Additive aggregation allows full compensation: a failure on one indicator is covered by success on another. Geometric aggregation limits compensation. TOPSIS assesses closeness to the best combination of indicators. The distance to it is denoted d⁺, and to the worst one d⁻. The distance to a benchmark compares a region with the combination of the best values reached by different regions.

A region enters the index if it has at least 60 % of the indicators. The weights of the missing ones are redistributed among the present ones.

correlation.title: Measures of association and significance testing
correlation.summary: The association between indicators is measured by the Pearson, Spearman and Kendall coefficients with the Benjamini–Hochberg correction for the number of comparisons.
correlation.limitations:
Association does not imply causation: both indicators may follow a third.
Regional sums are related through the size of the regions, so per-inhabitant values are compared.
correlation.body:
The Pearson coefficient measures linear association and is sensitive to outliers. The Spearman coefficient measures the association of ranks and is the default. The Kendall coefficient assesses the agreement of order in small samples. The coefficient is not computed on fewer than eight pairs.

A matrix of ten indicators has 45 pairs. At the 5 % level two or three of them will turn out significant by chance. So the p-values are ordered and corrected, and m is the number of pairs. Partial correlation removes the influence of the other selected indicators. The association line is a regression with HC3 robust errors, drawn when the slope is significant.

inequality.title: Measuring inter-regional inequality
inequality.summary: Regional inequality is described by the coefficient of variation, Gini, Theil with a breakdown by districts, Atkinson, the decile ratio and the Lorenz curve.
inequality.limitations:
Theil and Atkinson are computed only for positive values, Gini for non-negative ones.
The decile ratio relies on two points and misses changes between them.
inequality.body:
The measures are sensitive to different parts of the distribution, so a set is shown. Gini reacts mainly to the middle of the distribution. Theil reacts more to the upper part and splits into differences between districts and within them. In Atkinson the parameter ε (0.5 by default) sets how much the lag of the lower part matters.

Without weighting a measure describes the difference between regions. With population weighting it describes the difference in people’s living conditions. The dynamics of the measures are computed on a constant composition of regions. If some values are withheld, bounds of the measures are shown.

convergence.title: Sigma and beta convergence
convergence.summary: Convergence shows whether regions are drawing closer in the level of an indicator and how fast.
convergence.limitations:
One measure does not follow from the other: laggards can grow faster while the spread grows.
The conclusion depends on the ends of the period, and at least five years and 20 regions are needed.
convergence.body:
Sigma convergence is a reduction of the spread over time. The spread is measured by the standard deviation of logarithms. Beta convergence is a negative relationship between the average annual growth rate and the logarithm of the initial level y. Conditional beta convergence adds federal district dummies. It checks convergence towards the level of one’s own district.

The regression is estimated with HC3 robust errors. The half-life is the number of years in which half of the gap disappears at the same rate. Longer than 200 years it is considered practically infinite.

spatial.title: Spatial autocorrelation
spatial.summary: The global Moran’s index shows whether neighbouring regions are similar, and the local indices (LISA) show where the clusters and outliers are.
spatial.limitations:
The conclusion depends on the neighbourhood scheme, and one that holds under all three is more reliable.
The global index describes the country as a whole, not a single region.
spatial.body:
Neighbours w are set by one of three schemes. By default it is a common border together with bridges and sea links. You can take only the land border or the five nearest regions by distance. Under the land scheme the Kaliningrad and Sakhalin oblasts have no neighbours and do not enter the calculation.

Significance is tested by permutations: the values are randomly reassigned to regions 999 times. The smallest attainable significance level is 0.001. Reopening gives the same result.

vrp.short_definition: The value of goods and services produced in a region over a year, less intermediate consumption.
vrp.definition: The regional counterpart of GDP. The sum of regional GRP is less than the country’s GDP: part of the value added cannot be assigned to a territory. That is defence, part of financial services, import taxes. GRP per capita is usually compared.

per-capita.short_definition: A quantity related to the population or another base: per person, per 1000 inhabitants, in per cent.
per-capita.definition: Only such indicators are comparable between regions of different size. An indicator without such a base is called absolute and marked “abs.”. A place by it reflects the size of the region.
per-capita.synonyms: relative indicator, per capita, absolute indicator, abs.

poverty-line.short_definition: Cash income per person below which a resident is considered poor.
poverty-line.definition: Until 2021 this role was played by the subsistence minimum based on the cost of the consumer basket. Since 2021 the subsistence minimum is set from the median income. The method also changed in 2013, so breaks are marked in the poverty rate series.

real-terms.short_definition: A quantity in constant prices, adjusted for price growth.
real-terms.definition: Shows how the quantity itself changed without inflation. It is computed using the indices of real wages and incomes, of volume or of consumer prices.
real-terms.synonyms: real, in constant prices, in comparable prices, deflating

volume-index.short_definition: The change of a quantity in comparable prices relative to the previous year, in per cent.
volume-index.definition: Rosstat computes it for GRP, investment, trade turnover and services. The value of the current year is recalculated in the prices of the previous one. The product of indices over several years gives the real change over the period.

fixed-basket.term: Fixed basket of goods and services
fixed-basket.short_definition: A basket of goods and services, the same for all regions, whose cost Rosstat uses to compare prices.
fixed-basket.definition: The passport divides income per capita and the average wage by the cost of the basket of the same year. This is income in fixed baskets, a RegionLens calculation. Purchasing power in Rosstat’s terms is a different indicator.
fixed-basket.synonyms: cost of the fixed basket, income in fixed baskets

gini.short_definition: A measure of inequality from 0 at full equality to 1 at maximum concentration.
gini.definition: Equal to twice the area between the equality line and the Lorenz curve. On the site it describes the inequality of values between regions. It does not decompose by groups, and the Theil index is used for that.

theil-index.short_definition: An entropy measure of inequality that decomposes into between-group and within-group parts.
theil-index.definition: Shows the share of inequality due to differences between federal districts. The rest is due to differences between regions within a district.

atkinson-index.short_definition: A measure of inequality in which the researcher sets how much the lag of the lower part matters.
atkinson-index.definition: Shows what share of the total could be given up if the rest were distributed equally without a loss of welfare. The parameter ε is 0.5 by default. The larger it is, the more strongly the index reacts to lagging regions.

coefficient-of-variation.short_definition: The ratio of the standard deviation to the mean: the spread as a share of the average level.
coefficient-of-variation.definition: The simplest measure of differences between regions. It is dimensionless and therefore comparable between indicators in different units. It is undefined at a zero or negative mean.

decile-ratio.short_definition: The ratio of the ninth decile to the first: how many times the boundary of the top 10 % of regions exceeds that of the bottom 10 %.
decile-ratio.definition: Easy to understand, but it relies on only two points of the distribution. It misses changes between them. It is not computed if the first decile is zero or negative.

lorenz-curve.short_definition: A chart of the cumulative share of a quantity against the cumulative share of regions ordered by increasing value.
lorenz-curve.definition: At full equality the curve coincides with the diagonal. The more it sags, the higher the inequality. With population weighting the cumulative share of residents is plotted horizontally.

constant-composition.short_definition: Regions that have values in all years of the selected period.
constant-composition.definition: The dynamics of inequality and spread measures are computed on a constant composition. Otherwise new regions entering the series would change the measures by themselves. The “all regions” switch returns the calculation over all regions of each year.

hidden-bounds.short_definition: The smallest and largest value of a measure under any withheld values within the observed range.
hidden-bounds.definition: Manski’s approach to partially observed data. The width of the interval shows how much the conclusion depends on what the source did not disclose.

quantile.short_definition: A value that divides ordered values in a given proportion.
quantile.definition: Quartiles divide regions into four parts of equal size, deciles into ten. The median divides them in half. On the map there are five quantile classes by default.

median.short_definition: The value above and below which half of the regions lie, called “middle of the regions” in the interface.
median.definition: The median is not shifted by one outlying region. The Russia value of per-capita indicators leans towards large regions. So the median, the level of a typical region, is shown next to it.

interquartile-range.short_definition: The difference between the third and first quartiles: the width of the band holding the middle half of the regions.
interquartile-range.definition: On trend charts the shaded band is the corridor between the first and third quartiles. A region’s line inside the corridor means a usual level. Outliers do not affect the range.

percentage-point.short_definition: The difference between two quantities expressed in per cent.
percentage-point.definition: Unemployment that fell from 5 % to 4 % fell by 1 percentage point. Relative to the earlier level that is 20 %. So the site gives the change of indicators in per cent in points.

correlation-coefficient.short_definition: A measure of association between two indicators from −1 for an inverse relationship to 1 for a direct one.
correlation-coefficient.definition: The Pearson coefficient measures linear association of values and is sensitive to outliers. The Spearman coefficient measures the association of ranks and is the default. The Kendall coefficient is more reliable in small samples. Association does not imply causation.
correlation-coefficient.synonyms: Pearson correlation, Spearman correlation, Kendall correlation, rank correlation

significance-level.short_definition: The probability of getting the same or a stronger association by chance when there is none.
significance-level.definition: Denoted p, and an association is considered confirmed at p < 0.05. When many pairs are tested, some pass the threshold by chance. So in the association matrix the level is corrected by Benjamini–Hochberg.
significance-level.synonyms: p-value, multiple comparisons correction, Benjamini–Hochberg correction

sigma-convergence.short_definition: A reduction of the spread of an indicator’s values between regions over time.
sigma-convergence.definition: Measured by the dynamics of the coefficient of variation or the standard deviation of logarithms. A falling curve means the regions are drawing closer. It does not follow from beta convergence.

beta-convergence.short_definition: A negative relationship between an indicator’s growth rate and its initial level.
beta-convergence.definition: Estimated by regressing the average annual growth rate on the logarithm of the initial value. A negative coefficient means that regions starting low grow faster. Conditional convergence allows each district its own level.

moran-index.short_definition: A measure of spatial autocorrelation: whether neighbouring territories are similar in an indicator’s value.
moran-index.definition: Takes values roughly from −1 to 1. A positive value means clusters of similar values, a negative one a “chessboard” pattern. A value near zero means random placement. The result depends on the neighbourhood scheme.

lisa.short_definition: An index of spatial association computed for each region separately.
lisa.definition: Assigns a region to one of four types. “High among high” and “low among low” are clusters. “High among low” and “low among high” are outliers. A type is named only when the association is significant.
lisa.synonyms: LISA, local indicators of spatial association

partial-correlation.short_definition: The association of two indicators with the influence of the other selected ones removed.
partial-correlation.definition: If the coefficient falls noticeably compared with the pairwise one, the association was largely explained by third indicators. Most often these are population or the region’s level of development.

normalization.short_definition: Bringing indicators in different units to a common scale from 0 to 100.
normalization.definition: Needed before combining indicators into an index: roubles, per cent and years cannot be added. There are five methods, and the choice affects the final ranking.

topsis.short_definition: An aggregation in which a region is scored by closeness to the best combination of indicators and distance from the worst.
topsis.definition: The name stands for Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution. Unlike additive aggregation, the method accounts for the region’s profile, not only the overall level.

composite-index.short_definition: A summary score built from several indicators by normalisation, weighting and aggregation.
composite-index.definition: Three decisions determine the result: the method of normalisation, of weights and of aggregation. Any of them changes the order of regions. So how stable the places are is shown next to the ranking.

series.short_definition: A pair “indicator + breakdown”, the unit of analysis on the site.
series.definition: One indicator is published in several breakdowns: “total”, “urban population”, “rural population”. Values of different breakdowns are not compared with each other. Besides the dataset series, RegionLens builds series from Bank of Russia and Federal Tax Service data.

edition.short_definition: A Rosstat publication for a particular year, for example the compendium “Healthcare in Russia” of 2023.
edition.definition: The dataset is assembled from issues of Rosstat publications for 2022–2025. One value is printed in several issues and may differ between them. Issues of the bulletin, GRP tables and Bank of Russia snapshots are publications of the same kind.

revision.short_definition: A change of a previously published value in a later issue.
revision.definition: The reasons are a refined methodology, incoming reports, recalculation after a census. Repeating a value without a change is not a revision. The value from the latest issue is in force, and earlier versions are kept.

comparability-break.short_definition: The year from which a series’ values are not comparable with earlier ones.
comparability-break.definition: Arises from a change in methodology, territorial boundaries or the scope of observed units. Breaks are marked on charts so that a jump is not read as a change in the region. The passport does not compute a change across a break.

hidden-value.short_definition: A value not published by the source for confidentiality (code −77777777).
hidden-value.definition: The data were collected but not disclosed: the region has too few observed units. The value would reveal the figure of a particular organisation. The reason for the gap is kept and shown in the interface.

publication-status.short_definition: Whether the source continues to publish a series.
publication-status.definition: Marked for series where this is known. Rosstat has stopped publishing regional demography, and these series will not be updated. Bank of Russia and Federal Tax Service series are updated with every release.

series-splice.short_definition: Continuing a dataset series with values of another publication after a check over the common years.
series-splice.definition: If at least 90 % of “region × year” pairs are within tolerance, the link is full. Otherwise it is conditional: the series continues, but a comparability break stands at the joint.
series-splice.synonyms: conditional link, full link, source joint, series continuation

preliminary-value.short_definition: A value marked “prelim.” that the source will still refine.
preliminary-value.definition: These are values that a Rosstat issue calls preliminary, and values of the last year of an issue. A later issue replaces them with refined ones.

frozen-denominator.short_definition: The population of the last published year used in per-inhabitant values for later years.
frozen-denominator.definition: Rosstat publishes regional population with a delay. Per-inhabitant values for later years are divided by the population of the last published year. Such a value is marked as a calculation.
frozen-denominator.synonyms: denominator, population of the last year

year-to-date.short_definition: A sum or index from the start of the year to the reporting month, for example “January–July”.
year-to-date.definition: Lending is compared year to date with the same period of the previous year: individual months fluctuate with the seasons. The price index relative to December of the previous year is also cumulative.
year-to-date.synonyms: from the start of the year, January to month

same-period.term: Same period of the previous year
same-period.short_definition: A comparison with the same month or the same part of the year a year earlier.
same-period.definition: This is how monthly values are compared: their seasonal fluctuations are the same. Levels and sums are compared in per cent, shares, rates and indices by a difference in points.
same-period.synonyms: year on year, over a year

sme-register.short_definition: The unified register of small and medium-sized enterprises of the Federal Tax Service of Russia.
sme-register.definition: The Federal Tax Service keeps the register from tax reports and updates it on the 10th of each month. It includes organisations and entrepreneurs that meet the conditions on headcount and revenue.
sme-register.synonyms: unified SME register, SMEs, small and medium business

overdue-debt.short_definition: The part of loan debt not repaid on time.
overdue-debt.definition: The Bank of Russia publishes it together with the total debt at the start of the month. The share of overdue debt shows what part of the debt is not serviced on time.

oktmo.short_definition: The All-Russian Classifier of Territories of Municipal Formations.
oktmo.definition: In the source dataset the OKTMO code is unusable as a territory key: for all federal districts and the country it equals 00000000. So the site relies on its own directory with ISO 3166-2:RU codes.

okato.short_definition: The All-Russian Classifier of Objects of Administrative-Territorial Division.
okato.definition: A region’s code consists of eight digits, of which the first two are significant. For example, Moscow’s code is 45000000, Tatarstan’s 92000000. It is shown in the passport next to the ISO code.

territory-matching.short_definition: Linking the labels of your table to the regions of the site’s directory.
territory-matching.definition: Abbreviations, Latin letters inside Russian words and words run together are corrected. Colloquial and English names, ISO and OKATO codes are recognised. The site asks about an ambiguous label (“Altai”). The choice is remembered for later tables.

nested-territory.short_definition: A region that contains another region.
nested-territory.definition: The Nenets Autonomous Okrug is part of Arkhangelsk Oblast, Khanty-Mansi and Yamalo-Nenets are part of Tyumen Oblast. On the site’s map the oblast is shown without the okrugs. Its sum is obtained by subtraction, which does not work for a share or an average.
nested-territory.synonyms: Arkhangelsk Oblast with the okrug, Tyumen Oblast with the okrugs

absolute-value.short_definition: A sum for a region: the number of people, cases, roubles in total.
absolute-value.definition: Such a quantity adds up across regions, and a place by it reflects mainly the size of the region. For comparison it is divided by the population or the area.

featured-set.short_definition: Indicators in twelve themes by which a region is described in plain language.
featured-set.definition: The set is selected by hand from Rosstat, Bank of Russia and Federal Tax Service series. Each indicator has a checked direction, a short name and a unit. Only these indicators are assessed as “better / worse”.

polarity.short_definition: Whether growth of the value counts as an improvement.
polarity.definition: Growth of life expectancy counts as an improvement, growth of poverty as a deterioration. The direction determines the “better / worse” assessments and the reversal of the scale in the index. The map colour shows the quantity, not an assessment.

map-class.short_definition: A range of values coloured the same on the map.
map-class.definition: A region’s colour means the class its value fell into. The class boundaries and the method of division are shown in the legend. The same data look different with quantiles and equal intervals.
